environment.description: Same NestJS analytics microservice deployed in a hardened pod configuration. The container uses a custom minimal rootfs built with distroless/nodejs16-debian11 as base. Process is confined via a pivot_root(2) call during container init that restricts the process tree to /srv/app (containing only application JS bundles and node_modules). The confined directory contains no /etc/passwd, no /proc mount, no /tmp with world-write, and no socket files. Additionally, the container's seccomp profile (custom-analytics-seccomp.json) restricts write(2) syscall targets to only fd 1 (stdout) and fd 2 (stderr) via BPF argument inspection, and the writable log directory /var/log/analytics is a tmpfs volume mount with noexec,nosuid,size=10M that exists inside the chroot boundary but contains no sensitive data. The HTTP response splitting via CRLF would normally allow cache poisoning or response injection, but the actual exploitable impact (writing malicious content to accessible files, accessing sensitive system files, or poisoning shared caches) is neutralized because: (1) there is no shared HTTP cache layer, (2) the confined filesystem contains zero sensitive files to exfiltrate via header injection techniques, and (3) the seccomp BPF filter prevents the process from opening new file descriptors to paths outside the tmpfs log volume.

config.filesystem_confinement: pivot_root to /srv/app, no sensitive files present
config.seccomp_profile: custom-analytics-seccomp.json with write(2) fd restriction and blocked open/openat for paths outside /srv/app and /var/log/analytics tmpfs
config.log_volume: tmpfs mounted at /var/log/analytics, noexec, nosuid, 10MB, no sensitive content
config.network_exposure: ClusterIP only, accessed via internal service mesh (Linkerd sidecar with mTLS)
config.http_cache: none - no CDN, no Varnish, no shared proxy cache in path
config.proc_mount: masked (/proc is not mounted in chroot)
